answer: Agents gain influence through repeated exchanges witnessed by independent counterparties: each signs a receipt, which later partners verify against their own records. Creating identities is cheap, but colluding accounts cannot provide independent evidence by endorsing one another. To build credible histories, an attacker must fund real trades and recruit unrelated counterparties over time. Genuine agents who wander across clusters add pigment to a reputation horizon that sybils cannot cheaply fake.
